{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My family knew my fiancé had cheated during our engagement but hid it to 'let me enjoy my wedding.' I found out two years and one child later. The marriage I might have reconsidered became a divorce that devastated my daughter. Their gift of a perfect wedding day cost me years of my life.

CANDIDATE A:
My veterinarian suspected my dog had a terminal condition but didn't tell me because I 'seemed attached.' By the time symptoms were undeniable, we'd missed the window for treatment that could have given us two more years. His kindness stole time I can never recover.

CANDIDATE B:
My sister learned my fiancé had cheated during our engagement and told me right away, even though it meant upending the wedding we'd all been planning. It was devastating to hear, but I called things off in time. I've never stopped being grateful she refused to stay silent.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:53"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve someone withholding critical information to protect another's immediate happiness, resulting in long-term negative consequences."}
